description: Messaging infrastructure for the Compze framework including command, query, and event handling.
releaseNotes:
- **Deferred tommand handlers: an exactly-once endpoint's tommand handler that never runs in its sender's unit of work.** Declared with `ExactlyOnceEndpointBuilder.RegisterDeferredTessageBusHandlers(...)`, through a `DeferredTessageBusHandlerRegistrar`, or by overriding `ExactlyOnceEndpointDeclaration.RegisterDeferredTommandHandlers(IDeferredTommandHandlerRegistrar)`, with `ForTommand`, whose handler takes the inbox's stopping token or none. A tommand the endpoint sends such a handler is stored in the endpoint's own inbox within the sender's transaction, and handled in a unit of work of its own once the sender has committed: exactly once, what the endpoint sends itself in the order the senders committed, and tried again while it fails, as the endpoint's `RetryPolicy` says, without the sender waiting for it or seeing it fail. So work of several durable steps runs on one endpoint, each step's handler sending the next step to the endpoint itself, across crashes and restarts. A tommand another endpoint sends reaches a deferred handler as it reaches any. A tommand type has one handler, deferred or not. Sending to a deferred handler is refused before the endpoint has started, and once its stop has ended; one sent while the endpoint stops is handled when it next starts.
- **A handler's registration chooses whether its tessages keep their place in the order its exactly-once endpoint's inbox handles tessages in: `HandlingOrder`.** `ForTommand` and `ForTevent` on `TessageBusHandlerRegistrar`, `IExactlyOnceTommandHandlerRegistrar` and `IExactlyOnceTeventHandlerRegistrar`, and `ForTommand` on `DeferredTessageBusHandlerRegistrar` and `IDeferredTommandHandlerRegistrar`, take an `order`. `HandlingOrder.AsAdmitted`, the default, is the order as before: one at a time, in the order the inbox admitted them, so that one that keeps failing holds up those behind it. With `HandlingOrder.None`, the inbox handles such a tessage as soon as it has capacity, up to 20 at once, at the same time as any other: one that keeps failing holds up nothing, and its handler runs at the same time as the endpoint's other handlers. A tevent gives up its place only when every handler it runs gives it up. It applies where the inbox handles the tessage: one sent or published by another endpoint, and one a deferred handler handles. On SQLite, whose one writer takes one transaction at a time, handlings still take turns, each from its claim of the tessage to its commit: a tessage that gives up its place is handled while another waits to be tried again. The convenience forms that resolve a handler's dependencies keep the default. A class of a consumer's own that implements one of the three registrar interfaces must take the `order` in its token-taking form.
- **A handler's registration chooses how long the inbox's handling transaction may run before it times out: `transactionTimeout`,** on the verbs that take an `order`. Null keeps the 45-second default, the one every unit of work has. So a long step, such as one that waits a minute for a git worktree's removal, runs as an ordinary handler in a transaction of its own. It is at most `TransactionManager.MaximumTimeout`, 10 minutes unless the process raises it: a longer one, which .NET would silently shorten, explodes at registration, as one not longer than zero does. A tevent's handling gets the longest timeout of its handlers', the default counting for a handler that chose none. It applies where the inbox handles the tessage: a handler that runs in its sender's or publisher's unit of work runs within that one's timeout. A handling whose transaction times out rolls back, and counts as a failed try. A long transaction holds its connection and its locks for as long as it runs: on SQLite the one writer, which every other write waits for. Compze.Teventive.MemoryImageStateStore's 30-second waits, for a taggregate another unit of work holds for update and for a reload, don't follow it: a long handler takes its taggregates for update last. A class of a consumer's own that implements one of the three registrar interfaces must take the `transactionTimeout` in its token-taking form.
- **A handling's transaction timeout holds even where .NET 11.0.0 loses a transaction's own.** .NET can lose a transaction's timeout when threads start transactions with new timeouts at the same moment ([dotnet/runtime#136986](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/136986)), and the transaction then runs on past it and commits. The inbox's handling transaction has a timer of its own that rolls it back at its timeout, as .NET's would, whether its handlers chose the timeout or keep the 45-second default.
- **An exactly-once endpoint's stop waits, for up to 30 seconds, for the units of work sending a tommand to the endpoint itself to end, before it releases its process lock.** None of them commits once the endpoint's next process may run.
- **Works with the database packages of this release, such as Compze.Tessaging.Sqlite 0.6.0-alpha, and not with earlier ones:** their inbox admits what an endpoint sends itself.
- **An exactly-once endpoint's stop can let go at once: `IEndpoint.StopAsync(CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)`.** Without a token it stops as before: its inbox handles what it has received, for up to 30 seconds. Cancelling the token ends that, in whichever phase the stop then is, as for a process handing the endpoint over to its next one: the inbox handles nothing more, and the handlers of the tessages still being tried are cancelled, through the token they were handed, and roll back. Those tessages, and the ones behind them, are neither handled nor marked failed: the endpoint's next start handles them, in their order. A try that fails once the inbox's handling has stopped doesn't count toward the endpoint's retry policy. A class of a consumer's own that implements `IEndpoint` must take the token.
- **TessageBus handlers can take a `CancellationToken`, after the unit of work:** `ForTommand` and `ForTevent` on `TessageBusHandlerRegistrar`, `IExactlyOnceTommandHandlerRegistrar`, `IExactlyOnceTeventHandlerRegistrar` and `IBestEffortTeventHandlerRegistrar` take a `Func<TTessage, IUnitOfWorkResolver, CancellationToken, Task>`. The handler is handed the token of the execution it serves: for a tessage the endpoint's inbox handles, its stopping token, cancelled when the endpoint's stop no longer waits for its inbox; for a handler run within a send or a publish, the token given to `SendAsync` or `PublishAsync`; for a best-effort arrival, a token never cancelled. The handlers without a token are registered as before. The token-taking form is the one abstract member of each of the three registrar interfaces, and the form without it a default method: a class of a consumer's own that implements one must implement the token-taking form.
- **The token given to `IUnitOfWorkTommandSender.SendAsync` also ends the wait for a receiver to bind a tommand to,** where the send waited out the endpoint's handler-availability patience.
- **`TessageHandlerRoster.GetTeventHandlers` and `GetVoidTommandHandler` return handlers that take the token too.**
- **A testing host's at-rest wait no longer times out on a tessage whose receiver's next process handled it before its sender's next process redelivered it:** the receiver acknowledged the redelivery as a duplicate, and the wait counted it as undelivered for ever. Seen when a specification stops a receiver with a cancelled token while it handles a tessage, then starts both endpoints again.
- **Requires newer minor versions of other Compze packages:** Compze.Internals.SystemCE 0.14.0-internal (was 0.13.0-internal). Upgrading to this version upgrades each package listed here too, so their changelogs apply to this upgrade as well.
- **Requires exact versions of the Compze packages whose internals it uses:** Compze.DependencyInjection 0.11.0-alpha (was 0.10.0-alpha or newer), Compze.Tessaging.Abstractions 0.9.0-alpha (was 0.8.0-alpha or newer). Upgrading to this version upgrades each package listed here to exactly that version, so their changelogs apply to this upgrade as well.
